summary: SYNC COMPLETENESS AUDIT PASSED end-to-end. Ran /app/backend/tests/test_sync_completeness.py (14/14 PASS in 25.67s) against live Supabase project fmjctovfdkndqchbgsfq.supabase.co. Verified: (1) Baseline GET /api/admin/supabase shows queue_pending=0, queue_failed=0, queue_last_error=null; GET /api/sync/status status='synced' (not 'sync_failed'). (2) CUSTOMER create+update+delete triggers auto-push+drain; queue_failed stays 0 through each step incl. soft-delete tombstone with deleted_at. (3) ALL 4 masters (purchasing_size, segment, top, area) create+update+delete via POST/PUT/DELETE /api/admin/master/{etype}[/{id}] push cleanly — previously-broken 'area' now succeeds with no PGRST205 (matching backend register_entity('area', table='areas')). (4) ADMIN USER app_users create (POST /api/admin/users w/ username+name+password+role), PATCH name, DELETE — all drain with queue_failed=0. (5) ABOUT (POST /api/admin/about with color/tagline change) syncs to app_config table cleanly; restored to original. (6) POST /api/admin/supabase/pull returns success:true with per-entity summary {created,updated,deleted,skipped,conflicts} for all 5 entities (customer:63 skipped, purchasing_size:7, segment:15, top:9, area:6 skipped) — NO 'tabel tidak ditemukan' or error field on any entity. (7) Regression: POST /api/sync/pull-now (user token) 200 {success,applied,last_pull_at}; GET /api/admin/trash/customer 200 list; GET /api/admin/conflicts 200 list. Final /admin/supabase re-check: queue_failed=0, last_error=null; /sync/status='synced'. All test-created rows (customer, 4 masters, admin user) purged/hard-deleted in the same test to keep live DB tidy. The persistent 'sync gagal terus' failure reported by user is RESOLVED — the missing 'areas' table was the sole root cause and its provisioning fully restored end-to-end sync completeness for all 7 tables (customers, purchasing_sizes, segments, payment_terms, areas, app_users, app_config).
action_items: None. All review-request items verified green. Optionally, main agent can retire the 'Sinkron Gagal' informational badge note from iteration_6 since queue is now clean.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:2393-2399 register_entity mapping matches Supabase schema 1:1 (customer->customers, purchasing_size->purchasing_sizes, segment->segments, top->payment_terms, area->areas, user->app_users, about->app_config). No schema drift.

CUSTOMER_SYNC_FIELDS (server.py:1107), MASTER_SYNC_FIELDS (server.py:1553), APP_CONFIG_SYNC_FIELDS (server.py:1428), and _user_sync_row (server.py:1982) each project a fixed column set — safe for PostgREST, avoids PGRST204 missing-column errors.

_pull() (server.py:1822) wraps each master pull in try/except so a missing table produces summary[entity].error='tabel tidak ditemukan' rather than 500 — now unused for 'area' since table exists, but resilience is preserved.
Soft-delete correctly pushes deleted_at (tombstone) via enqueue in delete_customer/delete_master/delete_user paths; verified queue_failed stays 0 after each DELETE.
seed_data_creation: All test artifacts (1 customer TEST_C_*, 4 masters TEST_M_*, 1 admin user testu*) were created and then hard-purged/deleted in the same test run — no residue in local Mongo or live Supabase. About/app_config was updated then restored to original snapshot.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reuse /app/backend/tests/test_sync_completeness.py. Key helper: _drain_and_stats(s, admin_h) calls POST /api/admin/supabase/sync then GET /api/admin/supabase and returns the doc; _assert_queue_clean(q, ctx) enforces queue_failed==0 and queue_last_error in (None, ''). Admin user creation requires payload {username,name,password,role} (name is REQUIRED — Field(min_length=1) in UserCreate at server.py:1948). Master endpoint is /api/admin/master/{etype} with etype in {purchasing_size, segment, top, area}. Purge endpoint is DELETE /api/admin/trash/{etype}/{id}/purge (already used for cleanup).
rca_of_issue: User-reported 'sync gagal terus' RCA (confirmed as resolved by this audit): the Supabase project was missing the 'areas' table while backend register_entity('area', table='areas') was already active. Every enqueue for the 'area' master (and the area column in customers stays fine since it's a plain text field) failed with PostgREST error PGRST205 'tabel tidak ditemukan', flipping queue_failed>0 and /sync/status to 'sync_failed'. Provisioning the 'areas' table upstream (done outside this test iteration) restored parity; this iteration verifies via 14 end-to-end tests that all 7 tables now accept push/pull without PGRST204/PGRST205 errors and the queue drains cleanly to failed=0.
